meta.description: All disadvantages (Nachteile) and Bad Traits (Schlechte Eigenschaften) for TDE4/DSA4.1. GP refunds are stored as negative values. Bad Traits (marked is_bad_trait: true) have a numeric rating and work like attributes for tests. Total GP from disadvantages may not exceed 50; at most 30 GP may come from Bad Traits. [M] = Magical disadvantage.

disadvantages.name: Superstition

effects.description: Hero must act according to superstitions; failure requires a test or causes distress

disadvantages.description: The hero is deeply superstitious, following rituals and omens. The higher the rating, the more severely and often the superstition governs behavior. A test against the rating may be required to act against the superstition.

disadvantages.name: Albino

effects.description: Social penalties from appearance; penalties in bright light; pink eyes and white hair

disadvantages.description: The hero is an albino — white hair, pale skin, and sensitive pink eyes. Social penalties apply in many cultures, and bright light can cause discomfort.

disadvantages.name: Fear of [...]

effects.description: Must test against fear rating when encountering the feared thing; on failure, must flee or freeze

disadvantages.description: The hero has a specific phobia. When encountering the feared subject, they must test against the fear rating or be compelled to flee or freeze. Severity depends on rating.

disadvantages.name: Arcane Fear

effects.description: Hero is terrified of magic and magical beings; must test when confronted with obvious magic

disadvantages.description: The hero has a deep fear of magic and magical phenomena. When confronted with obvious magic, must test against this rating.

disadvantages.name: Arrogance

effects.description: Social penalties when hero must humble themselves or show deference; may refuse

disadvantages.description: The hero considers themselves superior to others. Higher ratings require tests to accept orders, show deference, or acknowledge failure. Social penalties with those who perceive the arrogance.

disadvantages.name: Astral Block

effects.description: Permanently reduces Astral Points; interferes with spellcasting

disadvantages.description: The hero's magical potential is partially blocked. Permanent reduction of ASP and impaired spellcasting. Level I: -5 GP; Level II: -10 GP.

disadvantages.name: Blood Frenzy

effects.description: In combat, hero may enter an uncontrolled frenzy when they or allies take wounds

disadvantages.description: The hero can lose control in combat when blood is shed. When triggered, they attack the nearest target (friend or foe) and cannot easily disengage.

disadvantages.name: Fear of Dark

effects.description: Must test when in darkness; on failure, panics

disadvantages.description: The hero fears darkness. Must test against this rating when in significant darkness.

disadvantages.name: One-Armed

effects.description: One arm is missing; severe penalties to two-handed tasks; cannot use shields or two-handed weapons

disadvantages.description: The hero is missing one arm. Cannot use two-handed weapons or shields. Significant penalties to tasks requiring two hands.

disadvantages.name: One-Eyed

effects.description: No depth perception; penalties to ranged attacks and fine motor tasks

disadvantages.description: The hero has only one eye, losing depth perception. Penalties to ranged attacks, reading distances, and fine motor work.

disadvantages.name: One-Legged

effects.description: Severely reduced movement speed; penalties to most physical activities

disadvantages.description: The hero is missing one leg. Movement is severely impaired (requires a crutch or prosthetic). Severe penalties to all athletic and physical activities.

disadvantages.name: Impaired Sense

effects.description: One sense is significantly reduced; penalties to related tests

disadvantages.description: The hero has a significantly impaired sense (choose which). Penalties to all tests that rely on that sense.

disadvantages.name: One-Handed

effects.description: Hero can only use one hand effectively; off-hand is non-functional but arm is present

disadvantages.description: The hero has a paralyzed, withered, or otherwise non-functional hand. Off-hand is present but cannot be used, effectively limiting to one-handed activities.

disadvantages.name: Vanity

effects.description: Hero prioritizes appearance and reputation; may refuse tasks that could harm appearance or prestige

disadvantages.description: The hero is vain about their appearance and reputation. Higher ratings require tests to do things that would harm their appearance or prestige.

disadvantages.name: Color-Blind

effects.description: Cannot distinguish colors; penalties to tasks requiring color identification

disadvantages.description: The hero cannot distinguish colors. Penalties to tasks requiring color identification (such as Alchemy, identifying uniforms, etc.).

disadvantages.name: Obese

effects.description: Reduced movement speed and athletic ability
Increased suffering from heat

disadvantages.description: The hero is significantly overweight. Movement is slowed, athletic activities are penalized, heat affects them more severely, and they cannot wear standard armor without modification.

disadvantages.name: Miserliness

effects.description: Hero hoards money; must test to spend money even when necessary

disadvantages.description: The hero is miserly. Must test against this rating when required to spend money; on failure, refuses or spends as little as possible.

disadvantages.name: Obsessive Justice

effects.description: Hero must right perceived injustices; cannot easily ignore unfair situations

disadvantages.description: The hero has an obsessive need for justice. Must test when witnessing injustice; on failure, must intervene regardless of danger.

disadvantages.name: Wanted I

effects.description: Hero is wanted by authorities; bounty placed on head; severe penalties if caught

disadvantages.description: The hero is wanted by authorities with a bounty on their head. Level I (-5 GP): minor warrant; Level II (-10 GP): significant bounty; Level III (-15 GP): major bounty with active pursuit. Severe penalties if caught.

disadvantages.name: Glass Bones

effects.description: Wound Threshold reduced by 2

disadvantages.description: The hero's bones are unusually fragile. Wound Threshold is reduced by 2, meaning they suffer wounds from much less damage.

disadvantages.name: Greed

effects.description: Hero is compelled to take valuables; must test to ignore gold and treasure

disadvantages.description: The hero is greedy for gold and valuables. Must test against this rating to ignore tempting wealth; on failure, must try to acquire it.

disadvantages.name: Vertigo

effects.description: Must test when at significant heights; on failure, freezes or panics

disadvantages.description: The hero fears heights. Must test when at significant heights; on failure, freezes, panics, or must retreat.

disadvantages.name: Violent Temper

effects.description: When provoked, must test to avoid explosive anger; on failure, attacks or acts violently

disadvantages.description: The hero has an explosive temper. When sufficiently provoked, must test against this rating to remain calm; on failure, explodes in anger.

disadvantages.name: Pathological Cleanliness

effects.description: Hero is compelled to maintain extreme cleanliness; difficulties in wilderness or dirty environments

disadvantages.description: The hero has an obsessive need for cleanliness. Must test in dirty environments; on failure, refuses to proceed or must clean immediately.

disadvantages.name: Prone to Illness

effects.description: More likely to contract diseases and slower to recover

disadvantages.description: The hero is unusually susceptible to illness. Disease tests are more difficult, recovery is slower, and minor infections become serious.

disadvantages.name: Short-Winded

effects.description: Each GP refunded reduces Endurance Points by 2

disadvantages.description: The hero has reduced endurance. Each refund of 1 GP reduces EP by 2.

disadvantages.name: Lame

effects.description: Significantly reduced movement speed; limps permanently

disadvantages.description: The hero has a permanent limp or walking impairment. Movement speed is significantly reduced and athletic activities are penalized.

disadvantages.name: Light-Sensitive

effects.description: Sunlight and bright artificial light cause pain and penalties

disadvantages.description: The hero is extremely sensitive to light. Sunlight and bright light cause pain, reducing combat effectiveness and perception.

disadvantages.name: Light-Shy

effects.description: Uncomfortable in bright light; prefers darkness; penalties in full daylight

disadvantages.description: The hero prefers dim light and is uncomfortable in bright conditions. Penalties in full daylight for extended exposure.

disadvantages.name: Fear of Sea

effects.description: Must test near or on large bodies of water; on failure, panics

disadvantages.description: The hero fears the sea and large bodies of water. Must test against this rating near or on large bodies of water.

disadvantages.name: Terrible Attribute

effects.description: One attribute is capped at a very low maximum; cannot advance above a certain value

disadvantages.description: One attribute is permanently impaired and cannot be advanced above a significantly reduced cap.

disadvantages.name: Night-Blind

effects.description: Cannot see in darkness; even dim light causes perception penalties

disadvantages.description: The hero is night-blind — even moderate darkness renders them nearly blind. Severe penalties in anything less than bright light.

disadvantages.name: Dietary Restriction

effects.description: Hero cannot eat certain foods (e.g., meat, specific ingredients); social complications

disadvantages.description: The hero has a significant dietary restriction (religious, personal, or medical). Acquiring appropriate food is more difficult in some situations.

disadvantages.name: Envy

effects.description: Hero is envious of others' possessions and status; may try to undermine or acquire what others have

disadvantages.description: The hero is envious of others' possessions, status, or abilities. Must test when confronted with something they covet.

disadvantages.name: Curiosity

effects.description: Hero must investigate interesting things; can be distracted by mysteries and unusual events

disadvantages.description: The hero has an insatiable curiosity. Must test when confronted with something mysterious or interesting; on failure, must investigate regardless of risk.

disadvantages.name: Low Astral Power

effects.description: Each GP refunded removes 1 ASP

disadvantages.description: The magical hero has reduced astral reserves. Each 1 GP refunded reduces ASP by 1.

disadvantages.name: Low Vitality

effects.description: Each 2 GP refunded reduces VP by 1

disadvantages.description: The hero has reduced life force. Each 2 GP refunded reduces VP by 1.

disadvantages.name: Low Resistance to Magic

effects.description: Each 2 GP refunded reduces RM by 1

disadvantages.description: The hero has reduced magical resistance. Each 2 GP refunded reduces RM by 1.

disadvantages.name: Claustrophobia

effects.description: Must test in narrow or confined spaces; on failure, panics

disadvantages.description: The hero fears confined or enclosed spaces. Must test against this rating in narrow tunnels, small rooms, or enclosed spaces.

disadvantages.name: Code of Conduct

effects.description: Hero must adhere to a strict code of behavior; violations require atonement

disadvantages.description: The hero follows a strict code of conduct (warrior's code, religious vows, knightly oaths, etc.). Cost depends on strictness (-3 to -12 GP). Violations have in-game consequences.

disadvantages.name: Vengefulness

effects.description: Hero is compelled to seek revenge for any perceived slight or injustice

disadvantages.description: The hero never lets a wrong go unavenged. Must test against this rating to let an offense pass; on failure, must plan or execute revenge.

disadvantages.name: Agoraphobia

effects.description: Must test in open, unenclosed spaces; on failure, panics or must retreat

disadvantages.description: The hero fears wide open spaces. Must test against this rating in open fields, large rooms, or exposed outdoor areas.

disadvantages.name: Slow Regeneration

effects.description: Heals fewer VP and EP per rest; wounds take longer to recover

disadvantages.description: The hero heals abnormally slowly. VP and EP recovery per rest is reduced; wounds take significantly longer to heal.

disadvantages.name: Sensitive Smell

effects.description: Strong smells cause discomfort or nausea; penalties in cities, around animals, etc.

disadvantages.description: The hero's sense of smell is overwhelmingly acute. Strong or unpleasant smells cause nausea and penalties. Automatic for elves (rating 6).

disadvantages.name: Dietary Laws

effects.description: Religious or cultural dietary laws; must follow specific food preparation rules

disadvantages.description: The hero follows strict dietary laws of their culture or religion (e.g., Novadi halal-equivalent). More restrictive than Dietary Restriction.

disadvantages.name: Spell Impediment

effects.description: Penalty to all spell casting tests; difficulty for a specific aspect of spellcasting

disadvantages.description: The hero has difficulty with a specific aspect of spellcasting (e.g., requires silence, cannot use the left hand, must speak aloud, etc.). Penalties to relevant spell tests.

disadvantages.name: Clumsy

effects.description: General clumsiness; penalties to fine motor tasks and some physical activities

disadvantages.description: The hero is accident-prone and clumsy. Penalties to tasks requiring fine motor control, and occasional mishaps at GM's discretion.

disadvantages.name: Fear of Dead

effects.description: Must test when confronted with undead or corpses; on failure, panics

disadvantages.description: The hero fears the dead and undead. Must test against this rating when confronted with corpses or undead creatures.

disadvantages.name: Unpleasant Voice

effects.description: Social penalties related to speech; penalties to Sing and social tests

disadvantages.description: The hero has an unpleasant, grating, or off-putting voice. Social penalties in situations where voice matters.

disadvantages.name: Unattractive

effects.description: Social penalties in situations where appearance matters

disadvantages.description: The hero is notably unattractive. Social penalties in situations where appearance matters.

disadvantages.name: Inaptitude (combat/physical talent group)

effects.description: Maximum TP for this talent group reduced; advancement column worsens

disadvantages.description: The hero has a marked inability for an entire combat or physical talent group (-15 GP). Maximum TP decreases and advancement becomes more expensive.

disadvantages.name: Inaptitude (other talent group)
disadvantages.description: Inaptitude for an entire non-combat talent group (-10 GP).

disadvantages.name: Inaptitude (all melee talents)
disadvantages.description: Inaptitude for all melee combat talents (-10 GP).

disadvantages.name: Inaptitude (all ranged talents)
disadvantages.description: Inaptitude for all ranged combat talents (-5 GP).

disadvantages.name: Inaptitude Swimming

effects.description: Cannot learn the Swimming talent at all; automatically drowns in deep water

disadvantages.description: The hero cannot swim and cannot learn the Swimming talent. Automatic for Dwarves. Not freely selectable.

disadvantages.name: Inaptitude Drinking

effects.description: Cannot consume alcohol; any alcohol causes immediate illness

disadvantages.description: The hero cannot consume alcohol. Any consumption causes immediate severe illness. Automatic for Elves. Not freely selectable.

disadvantages.name: Obligations

effects.description: Hero has significant ongoing obligations (debts, service, family duties) that must be met

disadvantages.description: The hero has significant ongoing obligations — debts, feudal service, family duties — that require regular attention and resources.

disadvantages.name: Prejudice

effects.description: Social penalties when dealing with the disliked group; must test to act fairly toward them

disadvantages.description: The hero has a strong prejudice against a specific group (culture, race, profession). Must test to treat them fairly.

disadvantages.name: Unworldly
disadvantages.notes: Specific areas: Possessions, Religious Devotion, etc.

effects.description: Hero is naive or inexperienced in a specific area of the world; penalties to related social tests

disadvantages.description: The hero is unworldly in a specific area (e.g., Possessions — does not understand ownership; Religious Devotion — blindly follows religious teachings). Automatic for elves in their respective areas.

disadvantages.name: Hideous Appearance

effects.description: Major social penalties; strangers react with disgust or fear

disadvantages.description: The hero's appearance is repulsive or horrifying. Strangers react with disgust; major penalties to social interactions.

disadvantages.name: Dwarfism

effects.description: Speed (GS) reduced by 2
EC from armor and load is halved before subtracting from Speed

disadvantages.description: The hero is significantly shorter and smaller than average, with stunted limbs. Speed is reduced by 2. Encumbrance from armor and load is halved before applying its Speed reduction.

disadvantages.name: Elvish World View

effects.description: Certain talents are Leittalente — they advance more cheaply but cost more to neglect. See Lea Elves culture for specific Leittalente.
Penalties when acting against elvish values and nature-connected worldview

disadvantages.description: An elvish disadvantage that comes with the Lea Elves culture. It designates certain talents as Leittalente (lead talents) that are cheaper to advance but have additional obligations. Specific lead talents are marked with (L) in the Lea Elves culture entry.
